items.passage: Because parents who value self-reliance are inclined to give their children distinctive names, economists Samuel Bazzi, Martin Fiszbein, and Mesay Gebresilasse treated the prevalence of infrequent first names in a US county as ______ individualism there. As late as 1940, such names remained more common in counties with longer histories of frontier settlement.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: A barometer of something is an indicator that registers how much of it is present. The text explains that “parents who value self-reliance are inclined to give their children distinctive names,” so the prevalence of infrequent names in a county rises with individualism there. That is why the economists could treat it as a barometer of individualism.

A.why_wrong: A repudiation of individualism would be a rejection of it. The text presents distinctive names as something chosen by parents who “value self-reliance,” so the names express individualism rather than reject it.

B.recipe: near miss: wrong direction of the relation (CONNOT)
B.why_wrong: An impetus for individualism would be something that drives people toward it. The text runs the other way: parents who “value self-reliance” choose distinctive names, so the names reflect individualism that already exists rather than produce it.

D.why_wrong: A prerequisite for individualism would be something required before it could exist. Nothing in the text suggests that people need distinctive names in order to be individualistic; the names are only a sign of it.

sources.what: Boston University article on Bazzi, Fiszbein and Gebresilasse’s frontier study: individualistic types are prone to give their children infrequent names, reflecting a desire to stand out (a names-based measure borrowed from social psychologists); as late as 1940, families in long-established frontier counties favored unusual names; longer frontier exposure linked to individualism and opposition to redistribution

items.notes: Subject: social science (economic history). Key letter C. Band-7 moves: a familiar word in a transferred sense (barometer, a weather instrument, used for a social indicator); the clue is a cause clause (Because ... distinctive names) one level more abstract than the key, so the student must see that a choice driven by self-reliance can serve as a gauge of it; near miss an impetus for fails only on the direction of the relation. Steps: 2. Raw freq.txt ranks (reviewer): a repudiation of 20,957; an impetus for 15,727; a barometer of 17,917; a prerequisite for absent (all four past 10,000, two past 20,000). Key not the longest option.

fixes: replaced distractors a deterrent to and a catalyst for (wording copied from model 3021d9ef: deterrents to, catalysts of) with a repudiation of (reversal) and an impetus for (direction near miss); rewrote their why_wrong
dropped markedly from more common (the BU source says only that frontier counties chose more unusual names)

band7.why: after the distractor swap all four options past rank 10,000 (two past 20,000), key a transferred sense (barometer as social indicator), near miss impetus for fails only on direction; logic is two steps with a cause clause rather than the model's concessive frame, so it sits at the low end of band 7

items.passage: Although attitudes toward women’s work outside the home are often assumed to be ______ a country’s present economic conditions, economists Alberto Alesina, Paola Giuliano, and Nathan Nunn found that among second-generation immigrants raised in the United States, women whose parents came from cultures that traditionally farmed with the plough were less likely to be in the labor force.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Contingent on means depending on. The word “Although” sets the common assumption against the finding. The “second-generation immigrants raised in the United States” all grew up under the same present economic conditions, yet women whose parents came from “cultures that traditionally farmed with the plough were less likely to be in the labor force.” That challenges the assumption that such attitudes are contingent on present economic conditions, since inherited culture made a difference.

B.recipe: reversal: the trait of the finding, not of the challenged view (ANT)
B.why_wrong: Impervious to means unaffected by. The finding, that women of plough-farming descent worked less even under the same US conditions, fits the idea that attitudes can be unaffected by present conditions, so “Although” would set the finding against nothing; the assumption being challenged must be the opposite one.

C.recipe: near miss: wrong direction of the relation (CONNOT)
C.why_wrong: Conducive to means helping to bring about. The text is not about whether attitudes help the economy; the assumption it challenges is that economic conditions shape the attitudes, which the comparison among second-generation immigrants tests.

D.why_wrong: Antithetical to means directly opposed to. Nothing in the text suggests that anyone assumes attitudes toward women’s work are opposed to a country’s economic conditions; the question the study addresses is what those attitudes depend on.

sources.what: Alesina, Giuliano and Nunn, On the Origins of Gender Roles: Women and the Plough (IZA DP 5735, published QJE 2013): to separate culture from institutions and markets they examine second-generation immigrants in the US, who were all exposed to the same institutions and markets; women from cultures that historically used the plough have lower rates of labor force participation in the US

items.notes: Subject: social science (economics). Key letter A. Band-7 moves: concessive frame (Although ... often assumed) with the blank on the view being challenged, and the finding’s own trait (impervious to) offered as a reversal; the student must supply the unstated premise that second-generation immigrants raised in the US share the same present conditions (three steps: undo the concession, see the shared economy, see that ancestry still mattered). Raw freq.txt ranks: contingent on 17,762; impervious to 20,091; conducive to 24,104; antithetical to absent (all four past 10,000). Key not the longest option.

band7.why: concessive frame with the blank on the challenged view, the finding's own trait (impervious to) offered as the reversal, an unstated premise (US-raised children share present conditions) needed; all four options past rank 10,000, as in model 1455b754

items.passage: The anatomy of Daphnia lumholtzi, a tiny crustacean first detected in North American reservoirs in 1991 and since documented in more than a dozen US states, is remarkably ______. Individuals exposed to chemicals released by predators grow an enlarged helmet and a long tail spine, whereas those raised without such cues are morphologically similar to other Daphnia species.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Malleable means readily changed in form. The text shows the species taking two shapes depending on its surroundings: individuals “exposed to chemicals released by predators grow an enlarged helmet and a long tail spine,” whereas those “raised without such cues are morphologically similar to other Daphnia species.” Anatomy that changes in this way is malleable.

A.recipe: near miss: true of part of the clue (CONNOT)
A.why_wrong: An enlarged helmet and long spine may be conspicuous, but the text’s point is the contrast between two forms: without such cues individuals “are morphologically similar to other Daphnia species,” so the species’ anatomy is not remarkable for being conspicuous.

B.why_wrong: Uniform means the same in every case. The text describes the opposite: individuals of this one species look quite different depending on whether they have detected predators.

C.why_wrong: The text mentions predators, but it never says this crustacean is especially vulnerable to them; it describes how the animal’s shape changes when it detects their chemicals.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Daphnia lumholtzi: a long tail spine, large helmet and additional spines are produced in response to predator kairomones; without them it looks morphologically similar to other Daphnia species; first detected in Missouri and Texas reservoirs in 1991; since spread to more than 16 states

items.notes: Subject: natural science (biology). Key letter D. Steps: 2 (compare the two conditions, then name the property they show). Band 6 by plan: plain key in the manner of variable (3.4) and homogeneous (3.8), with the clue in the next sentence; the near miss conspicuous is true of the predator-induced form but not of the species as the text presents it. Raw freq.txt ranks: conspicuous 6,466; uniform 4,122; vulnerable 23,199; malleable 51,674. Key not the longest option. Kairomones simplified to chemicals given off by predators.

fixes: virtually identical to other Daphnia species changed to are morphologically similar to other Daphnia species (the source's wording: looks morphologically similar); explanation and why_wrong A requoted
since recorded in changed to since documented in (keeps the hard tier's long-word share at CB's level after the change above); why_wrong A its anatomy made the species’ anatomy

band7.why: band 6 by plan: plain key (malleable) from a two-condition comparison as in 3.4 variable; near miss conspicuous true of one form only

items.passage: Most people consider calming down the best way to handle nerves before a stressful performance. Psychologist Alison Wood Brooks found, however, that performers need not ______ their anxiety to succeed: participants who reappraised their anxiety as excitement, sometimes just by saying “I am excited” aloud, outperformed those who tried to relax.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: To subdue a feeling is to bring it under control or quiet it. The text sets the common view of “calming down” as “the best way to handle nerves” against Brooks’s finding: participants “who reappraised their anxiety as excitement” outperformed “those who tried to relax.” Anxious performers therefore need not subdue their anxiety; relabeling it works better than quieting it.

A.why_wrong: To harness anxiety is to put it to use, which is what reappraising it as excitement does. Saying performers “need not” harness it would contradict the finding that those who reappraised their anxiety did better.

C.why_wrong: The text never discusses whether performers reveal their anxiety to others; saying “I am excited” relabels the feeling rather than disclosing anxiety.

D.why_wrong: Performers may anticipate a stressful task, but the text says nothing about whether they must anticipate their anxiety; it compares relabeling anxiety with trying to calm it.

sources.what: Brooks 2014, Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, Get excited: reappraising pre-performance anxiety as excitement (Europe PMC abstract, PMID 24364682): most people believe trying to calm down is the best way to cope; compared with those who attempt to calm down, individuals who reappraise anxious arousal as excitement perform better; saying “I am excited” out loud; karaoke singing, public speaking and math

items.notes: Subject: social science (psychology). Key letter B. Steps: 2 (undo need not, then see that the finding favors relabeling over quieting). Band 6 by plan: the negation is stated outright and the reversal harness is the natural positive word under need not, as in the band-6 negated models. Raw freq.txt ranks: harness 7,347; subdue 15,435; disclose 12,686; anticipate 10,355. Key not the longest option.

band7.why: band 6 by plan: negation stated outright (need not), reversal harness is the natural positive word, key requires undoing the negation and reading the finding as relabel over calm

items.passage:
The following text is from Henry James’s 1878 novel The Europeans. Felix has just told his cousin Gertrude that her sister, who is walking in the distance with a young minister, Mr. Brand, seems to enjoy his company.

And in the excitement of observation Felix rose to his feet.

Gertrude rose also, but she made no attempt to emulate her companion’s discovery; she looked rather in another direction. Felix’s words had struck her; but a certain delicacy <u>checked</u> her. “She is certainly not indifferent to Mr. Brand; she has the highest opinion of him.”
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “checked” most nearly mean?
items.explanation: Here “checked” means curbed, or held back. Felix stands up in “the excitement of observation,” and Gertrude, though she “rose also,” “made no attempt to emulate her companion’s discovery” and “looked rather in another direction.” The sentence sets her delicacy, or sense of tact, against the pull of Felix’s words (“Felix’s words had struck her; but”), so her delicacy curbed her from staring at the couple as he did.

A.why_wrong: To check something can mean to scrutinize it, or examine it closely, but Gertrude’s delicacy does not examine her; it keeps her from looking, which is why she “looked rather in another direction.”

B.why_wrong: To check a fact can mean to corroborate, or confirm, it, but nothing is being confirmed in this sentence; Gertrude’s delicacy acts on her, keeping her from following Felix’s gaze.

D.why_wrong: Felix’s words “had struck her,” so Gertrude may be unsettled, but “but” sets her delicacy against that effect; what the delicacy does is hold her back, as her looking “in another direction” shows, not disconcert her.

sources.what: Project Gutenberg #179, Henry James, The Europeans (1878): last sentence of the paragraph in which Felix rises to watch Charlotte and Mr. Brand, and the following paragraph, copied exactly (the dialogue before them summarized in the intro line)

items.notes: Subject: literature (novel, 1878). Key letter C. Band-7 moves: a common target (checked) in a sense that is not its first one; the key is a mid-frequency word rather than the plain synonym (stopped); two distractors are real senses of check (scrutinize, corroborate) and one is a scene word built from struck her; the clue words are themselves less common or used in secondary senses (delicacy as tact, emulate). Raw freq.txt ranks: Scrutinized 18,297; Corroborated 22,317; Curbed 26,637; Disconcerted 8,436 (three of four past 10,000). Key not the longest option. The Europeans is used in no official item of any skill and in none of ours; Henry James appears in no official transcript.

band7.why: Wharton/Beckett pattern: common target in a secondary sense, mid-frequency key (Curbed) rather than stopped, two real senses of check (scrutinize, corroborate) and a scene word (Disconcerted); three of four options past rank 10,000; the real-sense distractors fit the slot only loosely, as Situated and Realized do in 7f935017

items.passage: Literary scholar Myriam Chancy has suggested that the family of Haitian novelist Marie Vieux-Chauvet bought back unsold copies of her 1968 trilogy Amour, colère et folie because they regarded it as ______, since its depictions of civilians menaced by soldiers and paramilitary forces could be interpreted as criticism of François Duvalier’s regime and so invite reprisals.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Incendiary describes something likely to stir up anger or conflict, as if it could start a fire. According to the text, the trilogy’s depictions “could be interpreted as criticism of François Duvalier’s regime and so invite reprisals.” A book that might provoke a dangerous response from the government is one the family would regard as incendiary.

B.recipe: near miss: same evaluative family, wrong ground (CONNOT)
B.why_wrong: Lurid means shocking in a sensational way. Depictions of “civilians menaced by soldiers” might be disturbing, but the reason the text gives for buying back copies is political danger (criticism of the regime that could “invite reprisals”), not sensationalism.

C.why_wrong: Anodyne means harmless and unlikely to offend. A book that could be interpreted as criticism of Duvalier’s regime and invite reprisals is the opposite of anodyne.

D.why_wrong: Abstruse means hard to understand. The text says nothing about the trilogy being difficult; the family’s worry was that readers could take it as criticism of the government.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Marie Vieux-Chauvet: Amour, Colère et Folie (1968, Gallimard) suppressed and withdrawn from circulation for unclear reasons; Myriam J. A. Chancy suggests the family feared government reprisal due to the trilogy’s criticism of the Duvalier regime and suppressed distribution by buying back unsold copies; in Colère a military commander confiscates a family’s land, in Folie poets are trapped by local paramilitary forces

items.notes: Subject: humanities (literary history). Key letter A. Band-7 moves: B2 with the cause in a since clause in the same sentence (one sentence, as in the band-7 B2 models) and an evaluative key in a transferred sense (incendiary, literally fire-starting); near miss lurid comes from the same family of words for disturbing books but fails on the ground the text gives; the rest are rare. Steps: 2 (from feared reprisals to the book’s quality). Raw freq.txt ranks: incendiary 32,026; lurid 8,766; anodyne 30,763; abstruse 24,252 (three past 20,000). The passage attributes the account to Chancy, as the source does, since other accounts of the withdrawal differ. Key is the longest option.

band7.why: B2 with the cause in a since clause in one sentence as in 571cf537 and a756aa95; evaluative key in a transferred sense, near miss lurid from the same family with the wrong ground; three options past rank 20,000

items.passage: Ahuna Mons, a mountain about 4 kilometers tall, is the only obvious cryovolcano, or ice volcano, on the dwarf planet Ceres. Planetary scientist Michael Sori and colleagues propose that it is unlikely to have been ______, however: older cryovolcanoes may have flattened over hundreds of millions of years, as ice slowly flows, until they became indistinguishable from the surrounding terrain.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Something unprecedented has never happened before. Sori’s team proposes that Ahuna Mons only looks alone: “older cryovolcanoes may have flattened over hundreds of millions of years” until they “became indistinguishable from the surrounding terrain.” If such volcanoes existed earlier, Ahuna Mons is unlikely to have been unprecedented.

A.why_wrong: Ahuna Mons is described as “the only obvious cryovolcano” on Ceres, so it is conspicuous; saying it is unlikely to have been conspicuous contradicts the first sentence.

B.why_wrong: The text never discusses whether Ahuna Mons is still active or dormant; its argument is about older ice volcanoes that have flattened out of sight.

C.recipe: near miss: the trait of the older volcanoes (CONNOT)
C.why_wrong: Ephemeral means short-lived. The text suggests that ice volcanoes on Ceres do not last as visible features, since older ones “flattened,” so it gives no reason to deny that Ahuna Mons is ephemeral too; the point of “however” is that it was not the first.

sources.what: USGS publication page, Sori et al. 2017, The vanishing cryovolcanoes of Ceres (Geophysical Research Letters): Ahuna Mons is a 4 km tall mountain on Ceres interpreted as a geologically young cryovolcanic dome; other cryovolcanic features are less clear, so either cryovolcanism is recent or older structures have been altered beyond recognition; the authors test whether domes viscously relax (AGU release: older cryovolcanoes may have flattened out and become indistinguishable from the surface, as glaciers flow)

items.notes: Subject: natural science (planetary science). Key letter D. Negated frame (unlikely to have been) as in the medium B5 models; the reversal conspicuous is the natural word for the only obvious volcano, and the near miss ephemeral describes the older volcanoes’ fate. Steps: 2. Raw freq.txt ranks: conspicuous 6,466; dormant 16,629; ephemeral 21,660; unprecedented 14,344. Key is the longest option.

items.passage: Sociologist Annette Lareau found that many middle-class parents in the United States practiced what she called “concerted cultivation,” enrolling their children in organized activities meant to develop their talents. Children raised this way tended to be ______ adults in positions of authority: they came to see such adults almost as equals and grew comfortable questioning them.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: To be unintimidated by someone is to feel no fear or awe of that person. The text explains that these children “came to see such adults almost as equals and grew comfortable questioning them,” which is how people behave toward authorities who do not intimidate them.

A.why_wrong: Deferential to means respectfully yielding to. Children who “grew comfortable questioning” adults in authority and saw them “almost as equals” were the opposite of deferential.

C.recipe: near miss: wrong attitude behind the behavior (CONNOT)
C.why_wrong: Questioning adults might suggest resentment, but the text presents it as ease, not hostility: the children saw such adults “almost as equals” and were “comfortable” questioning them.

D.why_wrong: Children who regularly question adults in authority are engaged with them, not indifferent to them; nothing in the text suggests they did not care about such adults.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Concerted cultivation: Annette Lareau, Unequal Childhoods (2003); middle-class parents engage in concerted cultivation by attempting to foster children’s talents through organized activities; it encourages children to see adults as their equals, and children become more comfortable questioning adults

items.notes: Subject: social science (sociology). Key letter B. Restatement after a colon; one reversal, one near miss (resentful of) and one unsupported word, as the report gives for medium. Raw freq.txt ranks: deferential to 12,560; unintimidated by absent; resentful of 10,661; indifferent to 2,479. Key is the longest option.

items.passage: Armenian priest and musicologist Komitas was a remarkably ______ collector of folk music: spending summer after summer in villages of the Armenian countryside, where he built close relationships with the villagers, he transcribed more than 3,000 songs, though more than half of those transcriptions were later lost.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: A prolific collector gathers a great many things. The text supports this description: Komitas spent “summer after summer in villages of the Armenian countryside” and “transcribed more than 3,000 songs.”

B.recipe: near miss: built from half of the clue (CONNOT)
B.why_wrong: The text says that “more than half of those transcriptions were later lost,” but it does not blame Komitas for the loss; nothing suggests he was negligent, or careless, in his collecting.

C.why_wrong: A reluctant collector would be unwilling to do the work, but Komitas returned “summer after summer” and transcribed thousands of songs.

D.why_wrong: Unscrupulous means lacking moral principles. The text describes Komitas building “close relationships with the villagers,” and nothing suggests he collected songs dishonestly.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Komitas: Armenian priest and musicologist; spent summers in the Armenian countryside, building a unique relationship with villagers to gather songs; collected and transcribed over 3,000 pieces of Armenian folk music, more than half of which were subsequently lost (around 1,200 extant)

items.notes: Subject: humanities (music). Key letter A. Restatement after a colon; the near miss negligent is built from the later clause about lost transcriptions, which does not say who lost them. Raw freq.txt ranks: prolific 23,160; negligent 25,831; reluctant 6,398; unscrupulous 10,758. Key not the longest option.

items.passage: Darwin’s finches on the Galápagos Islands are threatened by an introduced parasitic fly, Philornis downsi. Because the finches readily collect soft fibers to line their nests, biologist Sarah Knutie and colleagues induced the birds to ______ their own nests: nests containing at least a gram of cotton treated with the insecticide permethrin were virtually parasite-free.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: To fumigate a place is to treat it with a chemical that kills pests. Because the finches “readily collect soft fibers to line their nests,” they carried cotton “treated with the insecticide permethrin” into their nests, and those nests “were virtually parasite-free.” The birds were, in effect, fumigating their own nests.

A.why_wrong: The text says nothing about birds leaving their nests; it describes them adding treated cotton to nests that then became “virtually parasite-free.”

B.recipe: near miss: true of the material, not of its purpose (CONNOT)
B.why_wrong: Soft cotton might insulate a nest, but the result the text reports is about the insecticide: nests with treated cotton “were virtually parasite-free,” not warmer.

D.why_wrong: To infest a nest would be to fill it with pests, which is the opposite of what happened: the treated nests were nearly free of the parasitic fly.

sources.what: Knutie, McNew, Bartlow, Vargas and Clayton 2014, Current Biology, Darwin’s finches combat introduced nest parasites with fumigated cotton (Europe PMC abstract, PMID 24801182): introduced nest fly Philornis downsi threatens Darwin’s finches; finches can be encouraged to self-fumigate nests with permethrin-treated cotton fibers; nests containing at least one gram of cotton were virtually parasite-free

items.notes: Subject: natural science (biology). Key letter C. Cause clause (Because the finches readily collect soft fibers) plus the consequence after the colon; the near miss insulate is what cotton does in a nest, but not what the result shows. The key is the paper’s own term (self-fumigate). Raw freq.txt ranks: abandon 5,885; insulate absent; fumigate absent; infest 39,719. Key tied for longest with insulate.

items.passage:
The following text is from George Gissing’s 1893 novel The Odd Women. Dr. Madden has just made a joke rather than answer a young guest, Rhoda Nunn, who asked him whether women should sit in Parliament.

[Dr. Madden’s] daughters would not have ventured to express an opinion on such topics when he was present; apart with Miss Nunn, they <u>betrayed</u> a timid interest in whatever proposition she advanced, but no gleam of originality distinguished their arguments.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “betrayed” most nearly mean?
items.explanation: Here “betrayed” means revealed. In front of their father the daughters “would not have ventured to express an opinion” on topics such as women in Parliament, but “apart with Miss Nunn” they let a “timid interest in whatever proposition she advanced” show. They revealed that interest; nothing suggests disloyalty or deceit.

A.why_wrong: To betray someone can mean to deceive that person, but the daughters are not deceiving anyone by showing “a timid interest” in Rhoda’s ideas; the sentence is about what they let show when alone with her.

B.why_wrong: To betray a friend or cause can mean to abandon it, but the daughters do not abandon their interest; they show it, if timidly, when “apart with Miss Nunn.”

C.why_wrong: To betray someone can mean to report that person to an authority, but the daughters are not reporting anything to anyone; they simply show interest in Rhoda’s propositions.

sources.what: Project Gutenberg #4313, George Gissing, The Odd Women (1893), chapter 1: Dr. Madden answers Rhoda’s question about women in Parliament with a joke; the paragraph that follows copied exactly from its second sentence, with [Dr. Madden’s] replacing His

items.notes: Subject: literature (novel, 1893). Key letter D. Abstract sense of an everyday word (betray as show unintentionally), with three distractors that are other senses of betray, as in 2.19 (assumed: Acquired, Acknowledged, Imitated, Speculated). Raw freq.txt ranks: Deceived 3,195; Abandoned 3,393; Reported 3,758; Revealed 2,383. Key not the longest option. The Odd Women is used in no official item of any skill and in none of ours.

items.passage: Norwegian painter Harriet Backer was a ______ artist. She worked slowly and methodically, completing only about 180 works throughout her long career, and she is best known for detailed interior scenes rendered in rich colors, with careful attention to the interplay of light and shadow.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: A painstaking artist works with great care and effort. The next sentence says that Backer “worked slowly and methodically” and painted “detailed interior scenes” with “careful attention to the interplay of light and shadow,” which describes a painstaking artist.

A.why_wrong: A hasty artist works too quickly, but Backer “worked slowly and methodically.”

C.why_wrong: The text says nothing about Backer rebelling against other artists or traditions; it describes how carefully she worked.

D.why_wrong: The text gives no sign that Backer has been forgotten; it says what she “is best known for.”

sources.what: Wikipedia, Harriet Backer: Norwegian painter best known for detailed interior scenes communicated with rich colors and the interplay of light and shadow; her work was both slow and thorough; produced just around 180 works

items.notes: Subject: humanities (painting). Key letter B. Restatement in the next sentence (slowly and methodically, careful attention). The source’s slow and thorough is paraphrased. Raw freq.txt ranks: hasty 3,745; painstaking 22,230; rebellious 9,434; forgotten 799. Key is the longest option.

items.passage: In 1897, Swedish explorer Salomon August Andrée and two companions attempted to reach the North Pole by hydrogen balloon, but their leaking balloon descended onto the pack ice after two days. For 33 years, the expedition’s fate remained ______: no one knew what had become of the explorers until a Norwegian expedition discovered their final camp on Kvitøya in 1930.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Something unresolved has not been settled or explained. The text says that “no one knew what had become of the explorers” until “a Norwegian expedition discovered their final camp on Kvitøya in 1930,” so the expedition’s fate remained unresolved for 33 years.

A.why_wrong: The text does not say the expedition’s fate was celebrated; it says “no one knew what had become of the explorers.”

B.why_wrong: A documented fate would be one recorded and known, but for 33 years “no one knew what had become of the explorers.”

D.why_wrong: Nothing in the text suggests that anyone exaggerated what happened to the explorers; their fate was simply unknown.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Andrée’s Arctic balloon expedition: 1897 attempt to reach the North Pole by hydrogen balloon; the balloon lost hydrogen quickly and crashed on the pack ice after only two days; the Bratvaag expedition found the remains on Kvitøya on 5 August 1930, the chance discovery of the expedition’s last camp

items.notes: Subject: history (polar exploration). Key letter C. Restatement after a colon. Raw freq.txt ranks: celebrated 5,437; documented 5,158; unresolved 58,607; exaggerated 6,194. Key not the longest option.

items.passage: In 2017, paleoanthropologist Jean-Jacques Hublin and colleagues reported that fossils from Jebel Irhoud, Morocco, belong to Homo sapiens and are roughly 300,000 years old, making them the oldest known remains of our species. The fossils’ faces are strikingly ______: they closely resemble the faces of people living today, though the braincases are more elongated.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Modern means like the present day. The text explains that the fossils’ faces “closely resemble the faces of people living today,” so they look strikingly modern even though the fossils are about 300,000 years old.

B.why_wrong: The fossils are old, but the colon introduces how the faces look: they “closely resemble the faces of people living today,” which is the opposite of looking ancient.

C.why_wrong: Fossils can be fragile, but the text says nothing about their condition; it compares the faces with those of “people living today.”

D.why_wrong: Weathered suits old fossils, but the text describes what the faces resemble, not how worn they are.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Jebel Irhoud: Hublin et al. 2017 dated the remains to about 315,000 years ago, by far the earliest known examples of Homo sapiens; the facial features resemble modern H. sapiens, while the braincase has an elongated shape

B.why_wrong: To master a skill or subject is to learn it, but Miss La Heu is not learning her pain; she is bringing it under control so that she can go on talking.

C.why_wrong: The pain did show when it “swept over her face,” but “mastered” describes what happened next, when she controlled it and “quickly resumed” speaking, not its being revealed.

D.why_wrong: To tolerate pain is only to put up with it. “Mastered” goes further: Miss La Heu brings the pain under control, and right away she “quickly resumed” with “Never mind!”

items.passage: A large log-jam repeatedly forms where Texas’s San Antonio River is shifting its course into a channel called Elm Bayou. Geographer Jonathan Phillips determined, however, that the jam did not ______ that shift. Instead, wood accumulates at the site because of the narrow, stable channels created where the river’s flow divides.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Phillips found that the jam is not behind the river’s shift: “Instead, wood accumulates at the site because of the narrow, stable channels created where the river’s flow divides.” The jam is a result of conditions at the site rather than the cause of the shift, so it did not trigger that shift.

A.why_wrong: The text is about what causes what; whether the jam made the shift visible is never discussed.

B.why_wrong: A pile of wood and a change in a river’s course are not compared in the text, so saying the jam did not resemble the shift adds nothing the “Instead” sentence answers.

C.why_wrong: A log-jam cannot measure anything; the text explains that the jam forms because of the channels rather than causing the shift.

items.passage: Household recipe books from early modern England have often been described as the work of women alone. Historian Elaine Leong argues, however, that most were ______ projects. items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Leong’s view is set against the idea that the books were “the work of women alone,” and her example shows one notebook “supplemented for decades by Mary, Henry, their children, and other relatives.” Books compiled by many family members working together were collective projects.

A.recipe: reversal: trait of the wrong party (ANT)
A.why_wrong: Solitary work is what the earlier description implies (“the work of women alone”); Leong argues “however” against it, and her example involves a whole family.

C.why_wrong: Nothing in the text concerns what the books cost; it is about who wrote in them.

D.why_wrong: The notebook was kept and added to by a family for its own use; nothing suggests the books were made for sale.
